set.outcome:
**The bench is the page now — no scrolling, no reading, no gate.** Open it and the microphone picker, the level bars and the record button are the first things there (measured at 1280: the tool sits at y 219–522, above the fold, with only the tab bar above it). Every word I wrote — the cause, the curl line, the diagnosis, and this task's own report, steps and tables — is one closed line at the bottom saying *How this was found*. Nothing was deleted; it is one click down.

**Press record and talk. That is the whole thing.** The button works from the first paint and opens the microphone itself — no live test first. The open device's **name is in bold beside the bars at all times**, and if this browser has already allowed the microphone the bars are already moving before you touch anything. Under them: *bars flat while you talk? pick another microphone ↑*. That is the answer to what happened to you — the wrong device was selected, and nothing on screen said so.

**A take that heard nothing now proves it.** Instead of whisper's invented sentence, you get: *“Nothing reached the browser — captured 0.000 peak, 0.0000 average on Fake Default Audio Input. Pick another microphone above and watch the bars while you talk.”* Whisper's raw answer is still shown, under a label that says it is invented, so “Thank you” can never read as a transcription again.

![a take that heard nothing, with its evidence](/framework/ai/2026-09-22/dictate-silence/shots/bench-silent-1280.png)

**Proven with two fake microphones at 1280 and 400, zero console errors in either.** A speaking one: record with no live test → *“Heard you: 3.7s of speech”*, 3720ms found, the JFK sentence back from whisper in 410ms. A silent one (20s of zeros): 0ms found and the evidence line above. And one more thing that was quietly broken — an append to this task's log used to blank a finished take back to “—” and close your microphone; the bench is now built once and put back untouched, proven by appending to the log with results on screen and watching them survive.

**Left open:** the speech floor (0.02 RMS over 120ms) is tuned to a quiet room with noise suppression on — two prototype fields (`speech_floor`, `min_speech_ms`) if a loud room needs it raised.
